Deprecated: residual-independence direction test on a data frame

Source: R/direction-test.R
janusplot_direction_test.Rd

janusplot_direction_test() was replaced by janusplot_direction() in janusplot 1.0.0, which takes the rows, basis dimension and method from a janusplot_fit() object. This alias runs the same test on the complete cases of two columns of data for one more release.

Usage

janusplot_direction_test(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  k = -1L,
  bs = "tp",
  method = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_permutations = 500L,
  linear_tol = 0.01,
  gaussian_alpha = 0.01,
  seed = NULL,
  n_min = 30L,
  n_max = 2000L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing both variables.

x

Character. Column name of the putative cause under the forward hypothesis.

y

Character. Column name of the putative effect under the forward hypothesis.

k

Basis dimension passed to mgcv::s(). Default -1L lets mgcv choose.

bs

Character. Spline basis passed to mgcv::s(). Default "tp".

method

Smoothing-parameter selection method passed to mgcv::gam(). NULL (default) uses "REML".

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). Significance level for the two residual-independence tests. Residuals are called independent when the HSIC p-value exceeds alpha. Default 0.05.

n_permutations

Integer. Permutations used to build each HSIC null distribution. Must be at least 99 – the smallest attainable p-value is 1 / (n_permutations + 1). Default 500L.

linear_tol

Numeric in (0, 1). A fitted smooth counts as a straight line when 1 - cor(fitted, x)^2 falls below this value. Default 0.01.

gaussian_alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). Significance level for the four Shapiro-Wilk normality tests used by the linear-Gaussian detector. Default 0.01.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for the HSIC permutation draws. The reverse direction is seeded at seed + 1 so the two null distributions are not drawn from the same permutation sequence. Also seeds the row subsample taken when the complete cases exceed n_max; with seed = NULL that subsample uses seed 2026, so it is reproducible in both cases. The subsample does not change the global random-number state.

n_min

Integer. Smallest number of complete cases on which a verdict is given. Below it the function returns "undecided" with reason_code = "n_below_min" and reason = "n below n_min", without fitting or testing. Default 30L. Samples below 20 complete cases are refused with an error whatever n_min is.

n_max

Integer. Largest number of rows used for the fits and the HSIC tests, which build n by n kernel matrices. Above it a random subsample of n_max rows is drawn (see seed). Default 2000L. The HSIC verdict depends on n: with more rows the test detects smaller departures from independence, so verdicts at different n are not directly comparable.

Value

A janusplot_direction object; see janusplot_direction().
